title: I Reported the Pool Gate Propped Open With the Serial on the Alarm

parts.text: I found the pool gate wedged with a flip-flop at 6:07 p.m., alarm silenced, serial plate visible. The HOA email that morning had begged us not to prop for convenience. I was thirty-three, no kids, still able to read a serial. I photographed the flip-flop, the plate, and the email. Then I sent it to the management address in the email, not the Facebook fight. They came, removed the wedge, tested the alarm, and posted a notice with the serial like it was a wanted poster. Convenience went home in one sandal. I swam my laps with a gate that closed. Serials exist so wedges have names. I do not need a medal. I need a latch. The flip-flop did not get a memorial.

social.video_title: The serial plate made it to the notice — Part 1/1
social.description: Morning email, evening wedge, management not Facebook. Have you stepped over a sandal on a pool latch?
